The class of decision problems solvable by a Merlin-Arthur protocol, which goes as follows. Merlin, who has unbounded computational resources, sends Arthur a polynomial-size purported proof that the answer to the problem is "yes." Arthur must verify the proof in [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] (i.e. probabilistic polynomial-time), so that
  1. If the answer is "yes," then there exists a proof such that Arthur accepts with probability at least 2/3.
  2. If the answer is "no," then for all proofs Arthur accepts with probability at most 1/3.
Defined in [[zooref#bab85|[Bab85]]]. An alternative definition requires that if the answer is "yes," then there exists a proof such that Arthur accepts with certainty. However, the definitions with one-sided and two-sided error can be shown to be equivalent (see [[zooref#FGM+89|[FGM+89]]]). Contains [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] and [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] (in fact also [[Complexity Zoo:E#existsbpp|∃BPP]]), and is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:A#am|AM]] and in [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qma|QMA]]. Also contained in [[Complexity Zoo:S#sigma2p|Σ2P]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:P#pi2p|Π2P]]. There exists an oracle relative to which [[Complexity Zoo:B#bqp|BQP]] is not in [[#ma|MA]] [[zooref#wat00|[Wat00]]]. Equals [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] under a derandomization assumption: if [[Complexity Zoo:E#e|E]] requires exponentially-sized circuits, then [[Complexity Zoo:P#promisebpp|PromiseBPP]] = [[Complexity Zoo:P#promisep|PromiseP]], implying that MA = [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] [[zooref#iw97|[IW97]]]. Shown in {{zcite|San07}} that MA/1 (that is, MA with 1 bit of advice) does not have circuits of size n^k for any k>0. In the same paper, the result was used to show that MA/1 cannot be solved on more than a 1/2 + 1/{n^k} fraction of inputs having length n by any circuit of size n^k. Finally, it was shown that MA does not have ''arithmetic'' circuits of size n^k. ''See also'': [[#mae|MAE]], [[#maexp|MAEXP]], [[Complexity Zoo:O#oma|OMA]].

name: MAC^0
title: Majority of AC^0
body: Same as [[Complexity Zoo:A#ac0|AC<sup>0</sup>]], except now we're allowed a single unbounded-fanin majority gate at the root. Defined in [[zooref#jks02|[JKS02]]]. MAC<sup>0</sup> is strictly contained in [[Complexity Zoo:T#tc0|TC<sup>0</sup>]] [[zooref#abf94|[ABF+94]]].

name: MA^cc
title: Communication Complexity MA
body: Here, Alice and Bob collectively constitute "Arthur", and the cost of an MA<sup>cc</sup> communication protocol is defined as the bit length of Merlin's message plus the communication cost of the ensuing randomized protocol between Alice and Bob. (Not charging for the length of Merlin's message would enable every function to be computed with constant cost in this model.) Does not contain [[Complexity Zoo:C#conpcc|coNP<sup>cc</sup>]] (first shown by [[zooref#kla03|[Kla03]]]). It is open to prove that there exists an explicit two-party function whose MA<sup>cc</sup>-type communication complexity is ω(n<sup>1/2</sup>).

name: MA_E
title: Exponential-Time MA With Linear Exponent
body: Same as [[#ma|MA]], except now Arthur is [[Complexity Zoo:E#e|E]] instead of polynomial-time. If MA<sub>E</sub> = [[Complexity Zoo:N#nee|NEE]] then [[#ma|MA]] = [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:C#conexp|coNEXP]] [[zooref#ikw01|[IKW01]]].

name: MA_EXP
title: Exponential-Time MA
body: Same as [[#ma|MA]], except now Arthur is [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] instead of polynomial-time, and the message from Merlin can be exponentially long. There is a problem in MAEXP that does not have polynomial-size circuits [[zooref#bft98|[BFT98]]]. On the other hand, there is an oracle relative to which every problem in MAEXP does have polynomial-size circuits. [[zooref#mvw99|[MVW99]]] considered the best circuit lower bound obtainable for a problem in MAEXP, using current techniques. They found that this bound is half-exponential: i.e. a function f such that f(f(n))=2n. Such functions exist, but are not expressible using standard asymptotic notation.

name: mAL
title: Monotone AL
body: Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]]. Equals [[#mp|mP]] by definition.

name: MA_POLYLOG
title: {{zcls|m|ma}} With Polylog Verifier
body: Identical to {{zcls|m|ma}} except for that Arthur (the verifier) has random access to the proof string given by Merlin, and is limited to running times of order <math>O(\textrm{poly}(\log n))</math>. This class was used by {{zcite|SM03}} to show that if {{zcls|e|exp}} has circuits of polynomial size, then {{zcls|e|exp}} = [[#ma|MA]].

name: MA'
title: Sparse MA
body: The subclass of [[#ma|MA]] such that for each input size n, there is a sparse set S<sub>n</sub> that Merlin's proof string always belongs to (no matter what the input is). Defined in [[zooref#kst93|[KST93]]], where it is also observed that if [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|graph isomorphism]] is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]], then the complement of [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|graph isomorphism]] is in MA'.

name: MaxNP
title: Maximization NP
body: Has the same relation to [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] as [[#maxsnp|MaxSNP]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:S#snp|SNP]]. Contains [[#maxpb|MaxPB]]. The closure of MaxNP under [[Complexity Zoo:P#ptas|PTAS]] reduction is [[Complexity Zoo:A#apx|APX]] [[zooref#kms99|[KMS+99]]], [[zooref#ct94|[CT94]]].

name: MaxPB
title: MaxNP Polynomially Bounded
body: The subclass of [[#maxnp|MaxNP]] problems for which the cost function is guaranteed always to be bounded by a polynomial. [[#minpb|MinPB]] can be defined similarly. Defined in [[zooref#kt94|[KT94]]]. The closure of MaxPB under [[Complexity Zoo:P#ptas|PTAS]] reductions equals [[Complexity Zoo:N#npopb|NPOPB]] [[zooref#cks99|[CKS+99]]].

name: MaxSNP
title: Maximization SNP
body:
The class of optimization problems reducible by an "L-reduction" to a problem in [[#maxsnp0|MaxSNP0]]. (Note: 'L' stands for linear -- this is not the same as an [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] reduction! For more details see [[zooref#py88|[PY88]]].) Defined in [[zooref#py88|[PY88]]], where the following was also shown:
  • Max3SAT is MaxSNP-complete. (Max3SAT is the problem of finding an assignment that maximizes the number of satisfied clauses in a CNF formula with at most 3 literals per clause.)
  • Any problem in MaxSNP can be approximated to within a fixed ratio.
The closure of MaxSNP under [[Complexity Zoo:P#ptas|PTAS]] reduction is [[Complexity Zoo:A#apx|APX]] [[zooref#kms99|[KMS+99]]], [[zooref#ct94|[CT94]]].

name: MaxSNP_0
title: Generating Class of MaxSNP
body:
The class of function problems expressible as "find a relation such that the set of k-tuples for which a given [[Complexity Zoo:S#snp|SNP]] predicate holds has maximum cardinality." For example (see [[zooref#pap94|[Pap94]]]), the Max-Cut problem can be expressed as follows:
    Given a graph G, find a subset S of vertices that maximizes the number of pairs (u,v) of vertices such that u is in S, and v is not in S, and G has an edge from u to v.
Defined in [[zooref#py88|[PY88]]].

name: mcoNL
title: Complement of mNL
body: Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], where it was also shown that mcoNL does not equal [[#mnl|mNL]]. See also: [[#ml|mL]].

name: MinPB
title: MinNP Polynomially Bounded
body: Same as [[#maxpb|MaxPB]] but for minimization instead of maximization problems.

name: MIP
title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof
body: Same as [[Complexity Zoo:I#ip|IP]], except that now the verifier can exchange messages with many provers, not just one. The provers cannot communicate with each other during the execution of the protocol, so the verifier can "cross-check" their assertions (as with suspects in separate interrogation rooms). Defined in [[zooref#bgk88|[BGK+88]]]. Let MIP[k] be the class of decision problems for which a "yes" answer can be verified with k provers. Then for all k>2, MIP[k] = MIP[2] = MIP [[zooref#bgk88|[BGK+88]]]. MIP equals [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]] [[zooref#bfl91|[BFL91]]]; this is a famous non-relativizing result. In fact, there is an MIP for [[Complexity Zoo:N#ne|NE]] where the verifier is quasilinear time [[zooref#cm23|[CM23]]].

name: MIP_EXP
title: Exponential-Time Multi-Prover Interactive Proof
body: The exponential-time analogue of [[#mip|MIP]]. In the unrelativized world, equals [[Complexity Zoo:N#neexp|NEEXP]]. There exists an oracle relative to which MIP<sub>EXP</sub> equals the intersection of [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]], [[Complexity Zoo:P#pnp|P<sup>NP</sup>]], and [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]] [[zooref#bft98|[BFT98]]].

name: MIP^ns
title: MIP with Non-Signaling Provers
body: Same as [[#mip|MIP]], except that the provers can have non-signaling strategies. MIP<sup>ns</sup> with two provers is equal to [[Complexity Zoo:P#pspace|PSPACE]] [[zooref#ito10|[Ito10]]]. MIP<sup>ns</sup> with polylogarithmically many provers is equal to [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] [[zooref#krr13|[KRR13]]].

name: MIP*
title: MIP With Quantum Provers
body: Same as [[#mip|MIP]], except that the provers can share arbitrarily many entangled qubits. The verifier is classical, as are all messages between the provers and verifier. Defined in [[zooref#cht04|[CHT+04]]], where evidence was given suggesting that MIP* does not "obviously" equal [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]]. MIP* contains [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]] [[zooref#iv12|[IV12]]]. By contrast, [[Complexity Zoo:M#mip|MIP]], the corresponding class without entanglement, equals [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]] (and even MIP[2,1] with two provers and one round equals NEXP). Even MIP*[4,poly] and MIP[5,1] contain NEXP [[zooref#iv12|[IV12]]]. MIP*[2,1] contains [[Complexity Zoo:X#xormipstar21|XOR-MIP*[2,1]]]. In 2012 it was shown that [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qmip|QMIP]] = MIP* [[zooref#ruv12|[RUV12]]] In 2020 it was shown that MIP* = [[Complexity Zoo:R#re|RE]] [[zooref#jnvwy20|[JNVWY20]]].

name: (M_k)P
title: Acceptance Mechanism by Monoid M_k
body:
A monoid is a set with an associative operation and an identity element (so it's like a group, except that it need not have inverses). Then (Mk)P is the class of decision problems solvable by an [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] machine with the following acceptance mechanism. The ith computation path (under some lexicographic ordering) outputs an element mi of Mk. Then the machine accepts if and only if m1m2...ms is the identity (where s is the number of paths). Defined by Hertrampf [[zooref#her97|[Her97]]], who also showed the following (in the special case M is a group):
  • If G is any nonsolvable group (for example S5, the symmetric group on 5 elements), then (G)P = [[Complexity Zoo:P#pspace|PSPACE]].
  • (Zk)P = [[#comodkp|coModkP]], where Zk is the cyclic group on k elements.
  • If |G|=k, then (G)P contains [[#comodkp|coModkP]].

name: mL
title: Monotone L
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone log-width polynomial-size leveled circuits. (A leveled circuit is one where gates on each level can depend only on the level immediately below it.) Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], who raise as an open problem to define a uniform version of mL. Strictly contains [[#mnc1|mNC1]] [[zooref#gs91|[GS91]]]. Contained in (nonuniform versions of) [[#mnl|mNL]] and [[#mconl|mcoNL]].

name: MM
title: Problems reducible to matrix multiplication
body: The set of all problems reducible to matrix multiplication. That is, the set of problems <math>P</math> that can be reduced to the multiplication of two square matrices can be reduced to <math>P</math> in linear time. Currently, the best known algorithm for multiplying two <math>n\times n</math> matrices is the [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppersmith%E2%80%93Winograd_algorithm Coppersmith–Winograd_algorithm], which has a time complexity of <math>O(n^{2.376})</math> {{zcite|CW90}}. Note that for the general problem, a lower bound of <math>\Omega(n^2)</math> is trivial from the number of elements being considered.

name: MMSNP
title: Monadic Monotone SNP
body: Defined in [[zooref#fv93|[FV93]]] as a subclass of [[Complexity Zoo:S#snp|SNP]]. There are three syntactic restrictions defining the subclass MMSNP, based on the form of the SNP formula defining the language: # The second order existentially quantified variables, known as the proof relations, are restricted to be monadic. (Monadic relations can be treated as sets.) # Any relations in the formula other than the proof relations must occur only negated (the formula is monotone). # No inequality relations can occur in the formula. MMSNP seems to obey dichotomy, by excluding languages that are [[Complexity Zoo:N#npi|NP-intermediate]]. This is still open but widely believed. Dropping any of the restrictions monotone/monadic/without inequalities allows NP-intermediate languages unless P = NP, since any problem in NP is polynomial time equivalent to a problem in each of these broader classes. MMSNP therefore seems to be a maximal fragment of NP where NP-intermediate languages are excluded. Every constraint satisfaction problem with a fixed target structure is expressible in MMSNP, and there is a polynomial time Turing reduction from every MMSNP query to finitely many constraint satisfaction problems. MMSNP therefore seems to capture the class of constraint satisfaction problems with fixed templates, [[Complexity Zoo:C#csp|CSP]].

name: mNC^1
title: Monotone NC^1
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone [[Complexity Zoo:N#nc1|NC<sup>1</sup>]] circuits (i.e. AND and OR gates only). A uniformity condition could also be imposed. Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]]. Strictly contained in [[#mnl|mNL]] [[zooref#kw88|[KW88]]], and indeed in [[#ml|mL]] [[zooref#gs91|[GS91]]]. Strictly contains [[#mtc0|mTC<sup>0</sup>]] [[zooref#yao89|[Yao89]]].

name: mNL
title: Monotone NL
body: See [[#mp|mP]] for the definition of a monotone nondeterministic Turing machine, due to [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]]. mNL is the class of decision problems solvable by a monotone nondeterministic log-space Turing machine. mNL does not equal [[#mconl|mcoNL]] [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], in contrast to the case for [[Complexity Zoo:N#nl|NL]] and [[Complexity Zoo:C#conl|coNL]]. Also, mNL strictly contains [[#mnc1|mNC<sup>1</sup>]] [[zooref#kw88|[KW88]]]. See also: [[#ml|mL]].

name: mNP
title: Monotone NP
body: The class of decision problems for which a 'yes' answer can be verified in [[#mp|mP]] (that is, monotone polynomial-time). The monotonicity requirement applies only to the input bits, not to the bits that are guessed nondeterministically. So, in the corresponding circuit, one can have NOT gates so long as they depend only on the nondeterministic guess bits. Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], where it was also shown that mNP is 'trivial': that is, it contains exactly the monotone problems in [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]]. Strictly contains [[#mp|mP]] [[zooref#raz85|[Raz85]]].

name: Mod_kL
title: Mod-k L
body: Has the same relation to [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] as [[#modkp|Mod<sub>k</sub>P]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. For any prime k, Mod<sub>k</sub>L contains [[Complexity Zoo:S#sl|SL]] [[zooref#kw93|[KW93]]]. For any prime k, Mod<sub>k</sub>L<sup>ModkL</sup> = Mod<sub>k</sub>L [[zooref#hrv00|[HRV00]]]. For any k>1, contains [[Complexity Zoo:L#logfew|LogFew]] [[zooref#bdh92|[BDH+92]]].

name: Mod_kP
title: Mod-k Polynomial-Time
body: For any k>1: The class of decision problems solvable by an [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] machine such that the number of accepting paths is divisible by k, if and only if the answer is "no." Mod<sub>2</sub>P is more commonly known as [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]] "parity-P." For every k, Mod<sub>k</sub>P contains [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|graph isomorphism]] [[zooref#ak02|[AK02]]]. Defined in [[zooref#ch89|[CH89]]], [[zooref#her90|[Her90]]]. [[zooref#her90|[Her90]]] and [[zooref#bg92|[BG92]]] showed that Mod<sub>k</sub>P is the set of unions of languages in Mod<sub>p</sub>P for each prime p that divides k. In particular, if p is prime, then Mod<sub>p</sub>P = Mod<sub>p^m</sub>P for all positive integers m. A further fact is that Mod<sub>p</sub>P is closed under union, intersection, and complement, and low for itself, for p prime. On the other hand, if k is not a prime power, then there exists an oracle relative to which Mod<sub>k</sub>P is not closed under intersection or complement [[zooref#bbr94|[BBR94]]]. For prime p, there exists an oracle relative to which Mod<sub>p</sub>P does not contain [[Complexity Zoo:E#eqp|EQP]] [[zooref#gv02|[GV02]]].

name: ModL
title: Mod{{zcls|l|l}}
body: A language <math>L\in\mathsf{ModL}</math> if there are functions <math>f\in\mathsf{GapL}</math> and <math>g\in\mathsf{FL}</math> such that for all strings <math>x</math>: * There exists a prime <math>p</math> and a natural number <math>\alpha</math> such that <math>g(x)=0^{p^{\alpha}}</math>. * <math>x\in L</math> if and only if <math>f(x)\equiv0(\left|g(x)\right|)</math>. Thus, for any prime <math>p</math> and natural number <math>\alpha</math>, <math>\mathsf{Mod}_{p^{\alpha}}\mathsf{L}\subseteq\mathsf{ModL}</math>. Moreover, {{zcls|f|fl}}<sup>ModL</sup> = {{zcls|f|fl}}<sup>{{zcls|g|gapl|GapL}}</sup> {{zcite|AV04}}. Defined in {{zcite|AV04}}.

name: ModP
title: Mod_kP With Arbitrary k
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a [[#modkp|Mod<sub>k</sub>P]] machine where k can vary depending on the input. The only requirement is that 0<sup>k</sup> be computable in polynomial time. Defined in [[zooref#kt96|[KT96]]], where it was also shown that ModP is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:A#ampmp|AmpMP]].

name: ModPH
title: Modular Counting Hierarchy
body: The closure of [[#p|P]] under the ∃, ∀, and Mod<sub>''k''</sub> operators. Equivalently, the smallest class ''C'' such that NP<sup>''C''</sup>, coNP<sup>''C''</sup>, and Mod<sub>''k''</sub>P<sup>''C''</sup> are included in ''C'' for each ''k''. Introduced in [[zooref#gkr95|[GKR+95]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:P#ph|PH]] and [[#modkp|Mod<sub>''k''</sub>P]] for each ''k''. Contained in, and low for, [[Complexity Zoo:A#ampmp|AmpMP]] and [[#mp2|MP]]. For a fixed ''m'', the restriction of the class that only allows Mod<sub>''k''</sub> for ''k'' = ''m'' is denoted ModPH<sub>''m''</sub> [[zooref#buss17|[Buss17]]]. Toda’s theorem [[zooref#tod89|[Tod89]]] implies that for prime ''m'', ModPH<sub>''m''</sub> = BP·Mod<sub>''m''</sub>P.

name: ModZ_kL
title: Restricted Mod_kL
body:
The class of decision problems solvable by a nondeterministic logspace Turing machine, such that
  1. If the answer is "yes," then the number of accepting paths is not congruent to 0 mod k.
  2. If the answer is "no," then there are no accepting paths.
Defined in [[zooref#bdh92|[BDH+92]]], where it was also shown that ModZkL contains [[Complexity Zoo:L#logfewnl|LogFewNL]] for all k>1. Contained in [[#modkl|ModkL]] and in [[Complexity Zoo:N#nl|NL]].

name: mP
title: Monotone P
body: The definition of this class, due to [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], is not obvious. First, a monotone nondeterministic Turing machine is one such that, whenever it can make a transition with a 0 on its input tape, it can also make that same transition with a 1 on its input tape. (This restriction does not apply to the work tape.) A monotone alternating Turing machine is subject to the restriction that it can only reference an input bit x by, "there exists a z at most x," or "for all z at least x." Then applying the result of [[zooref#cks81|[CKS81]]] that [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[Complexity Zoo:A#al|AL]], mP is defined to be [[#mal|mAL]]: the class of decision problems solvable by a monotone alternating log-space Turing machine. Actually there's a caveat: A monotone Turing machine or circuit can first negate the entire input, then perform a monotone computation. That way it becomes meaningful to talk about whether a monotone complexity class is closed under complement. Strictly contained in [[#mnp|mNP]] [[zooref#raz85|[Raz85]]]. Deciding whether a bipartite graph has a perfect matching, despite being both a monotone problem and in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]], requires monotone circuits of superpolynomial size [[zooref#raz85b|[Raz85b]]]. Letting MONO be the class of monotone problems, it follows that mP is strictly contained in MONO ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. See also: [[#mnc1|mNC1]], [[#ml|mL]], [[#mnl|mNL]], [[#mconl|mcoNL]].

name: MP
title: Middle-Bit P
body: The class of decision problems such that for some [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#sharpp|#P]] function f, the answer on input x is 'yes' if and only if the middle bit of f(x) is 1. Defined in [[zooref#gkr95|[GKR+95]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:A#ampmp|AmpMP]], and [[#modph|ModPH]], which is low for both AmpMP and MP. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:P#psharpp1|P<sup>#P[1]</sup>]]. MP with [[#modp|ModP]] oracle equals MP with [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#sharpp|#P]] oracle [[zooref#kt96|[KT96]]].

name: MPC
title: Monotone Planar Circuits
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone stratified planar circuits (a uniformity condition may also be imposed). Such a circuit can contain only AND and OR gates of bounded fanin. It must be embeddable in the plane with no wires crossing. Furthermore, the input bits can only be accessed at the bottom level, where they are listed in order (x1,...,xn). Defined in [[zooref#dc89|[DC89]]]. [[zooref#blm99|[BLM+99]]] showed that we can assume without loss of generality that the circuit has width n and depth n3.

name: mP/poly
title: Monotone P/poly
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a nonuniform family of polynomial-size Boolean circuits with only AND and OR gates, no NOT gates. (Or rather, following the definitions of [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]], the entire input can be negated as long as there are no other negations.) More straightforward to define than [[#mp|mP]].

name: mTC^0
title: Monotone TC^0
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a family of monotone [[Complexity Zoo:T#tc0|TC<sup>0</sup>]] circuits (i.e. constant-depth, polynomial-size, AND, OR, and threshold gates, but no NOT gates). A uniformity condition could also be imposed. Defined in [[zooref#gs90|[GS90]]]. Strictly contained in [[#mnc1|mNC<sup>1</sup>]] [[zooref#yao89|[Yao89]]].

name: naCQP
title: non-adaptive Collapse-free Quantum Polynomial time
body: Defined in the conference version of [[zooref#abfl14|[ABFL14]]]. Same as [[Complexity Zoo:P#pdqp|PDQP]].

name: NAuxPDA^p
title: Nondeterministic Auxiliary Pushdown Automata
body: The class of problems solvable by nondeterministic logarithmic-space and polynomial-time Turing machines with auxiliary pushdown. Equals [[Complexity Zoo:L#logcfl|LOGCFL]] [[zooref#sud78|[Sud78]]].

name: NC
title: Nick's Class
body: (Named in honor of Nick Pippenger.) NC<sup>i</sup> is the class of decision problems solvable by a uniform family of Boolean circuits, with polynomial size, depth O(log<sup>i</sup>(n)), and fan-in 2. Then NC is the union of NC<sup>i</sup> over all nonnegative i. Also, NC equals the union of [[Complexity Zoo:P#ptwk|PT/WK]](log<sup>k</sup>n, n<sup>k</sup>)/poly over all constants k. NC<sup>i</sup> is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:A#ac|AC]]<sup>i</sup>; thus, NC = [[Complexity Zoo:A#ac|AC]]. Contains [[#nl|NL]], in fact [[#nl|NL]] is contained in [[#nc2|NC<sup>2</sup>]]. Generalizations include [[Complexity Zoo:R#rnc|RNC]] and [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qnc|QNC]]. [[zooref#in96|[IN96]]] construct a candidate pseudorandom generator in NC based on the subset sum problem. For a random oracle A, (NC<sup>i</sup>)<sup>A</sup> is strictly contained in (NC<sup>i+1</sup>)<sup>A</sup>, and uniform NC<sup>A</sup> is strictly contained in P<sup>A</sup>, with probability 1 [[zooref#mil92|[Mil92]]]. In descriptive complexity, NC can be defined by [[Complexity_Zoo:F#fot|FO[<math> \log(n)^{O(1)}</math>]]] Log space uniform NC is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:A#atime|ATIME]](poly(log(n))) = [[Complexity Zoo:P#polyl|polyL]] [[zooref#ruz81|[RUZ81]]].

name: NC^0
title: Level 0 of NC
body: By definition, a decision problem in NC0 can depend on only a constant number of bits of the input. Thus, NC0 usually refers to functions computable by constant-depth, bounded-fanin circuits. There is a family of permutations computable by a uniform family of NC0 circuits that is [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]-hard to invert [[zooref#has88|[Has88]]]. Recently [[zooref#aik04|[AIK04]]] solved a longstanding open problem by showing that there exist pseudorandom generators and one-way functions in NC0, based on (for example) the hardness of [[Complexity_Garden#integer_factorization|factoring]]. Specifically, in these generators every bit of the output depends on only 4 input bits. Whether the dependence can be reduced to 3 bits under the same cryptographic assumptions is open, but [[zooref#aik04|[AIK04]]] have some partial results in this direction. It is known that the dependence cannot be reduced to 2 bits.

name: NC^1
title: Level 1 of NC
body: See [[#nc|NC]] for definition. [[zooref#kv94|[KV94]]] give a family of functions that is computable in NC1, but not efficiently learnable unless there exists an efficient algorithm for factoring Blum integers. Was shown to equal 5-[[Complexity Zoo:P#kpbp|PBP]] [[zooref#bar89|[Bar89]]]. On the other hand, width 5 is necessary unless NC1 = [[Complexity Zoo:A#acc0|ACC0]] [[zooref#bt88|[BT88]]]. As an application of this result, NC1 can be simulated on a quantum computer with three qubits, one initialized to a pure state and the remaining two in the maximally mixed state [[zooref#asv00|[ASV00]]]. Surprisingly, [[zooref#amp02|[AMP02]]] showed that only a single qubit is needed to simulate NC1 - i.e. that NC1 is contained in 2-[[Complexity Zoo:E#eqbp|EQBP]]. (Complex amplitudes are needed for this result.) Is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] [[zooref#bor77|[Bor77]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:T#tc0|TC0]]. NC1 contains the integer division problem [[zooref#bch86|[BCH86]]], even if an [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]]-uniformity condition is imposed [[zooref#cdl01|[CDL01]]]. UE*-uniform NC1 is equal to [[Complexity Zoo:A#alogtime|ALOGTIME]] [[zooref#ruz81|[RUZ81]]].

name: NC^2
title: Level 2 of NC
body: See [[#nc|NC]] for definition. Contains [[Complexity_Zoo:A#ac1|AC<sup>1</sup>]] and [[Complexity Zoo:D#det|DET]], both of which contain [[#nl|NL]]. It seems we currently (as of this writing, 15 Jun 2022) do not know any problem in NC<sup>2</sup> that's not known to be in [[Complexity_Zoo:A#ac1|AC<sup>1</sup>]]∪ [[Complexity Zoo:D#det|DET]] (see [https://cstheory.stackexchange.com/q/39831/129 this question]).

name: NE
title: Nondeterministic E
body: Nondeterministic exponential time with linear exponent (i.e. [[#ntime|NTIME]](2<sup>O(n)</sup>)). [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]<sup>NE</sup> = [[#np|NP]]<sup>NE</sup> [[zooref#hem89|[Hem89]]]. Contained in [[#nexp|NEXP]]. Has an [[Complexity Zoo:M#mip|MIP]] where the verifier is quasilinear time [[zooref#cm23|[CM23]]].

name: Nearly-P
title: Languages Superpolynomially Close to P
body: The set of languages L such that for every k, there is a language L_k in P that differs from L on at most 2<sup>n</sup>/n<sup>k</sup> inputs of length n. Discussed in [[zooref#ns05|[NS05]]] and implicitly defined in [[zooref#yam99|[Yam99]]].

name: NEE
title: Nondeterministic EE
body: Nondeterministic double-exponential time with linear exponent (i.e. [[#ntime|NTIME]](2<sup>2<sup>O(n)</sup></sup>)). If [[Complexity Zoo:M#mae|MA<sub>E</sub>]] = NEE then [[Complexity Zoo:M#ma|MA]] = [[#nexp|NEXP]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:C#conexp|coNEXP]] [[zooref#ikw01|[IKW01]]]. Contained in [[#neexp|NEEXP]].

name: NEEE
title: Nondeterministic EEE
body: Nondeterministic triple-exponential time with linear exponent.

name: NEEXP
title: Nondeterministic EEXP
body: Nondeterministic double-exponential time (i.e. [[#ntime|NTIME]](2<sup>2<sup>p(n)</sup></sup>) for p a polynomial). Equals [[Complexity Zoo:M#mipexp|MIP<sub>EXP</sub>]] (unrelativized).

name: NE/poly
title: Nonuniform NE
body: Contains [[Complexity Zoo:C#cone|coNE]], just as [[#nexppoly|NEXP/poly]] contains [[Complexity Zoo:C#conexp|coNEXP]].

name: NEXP
title: Nondeterministic EXP
body:
Nondeterministic exponential time (i.e. [[#ntime|NTIME]](2p(n)) for p a polynomial). Equals [[Complexity Zoo:M#mip|MIP]] [[zooref#bfl91|[BFL91]]] (but not relative to all oracles). NEXP is in [[Complexity Zoo:M#mipstar|MIP*]] [[zooref#iv12|[IV12]]]. NEXP is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] if and only if NEXP = [[Complexity Zoo:M#ma|MA]] [[zooref#ikw01|[IKW01]]]. [[zooref#ki02|[KI02]]] show the following:
  • If [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[Complexity Zoo:R#rp|RP]], then NEXP is not computable by polynomial-size arithmetic circuits.
  • If [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] and if checking whether a Boolean circuit computes a function that is close to a low-degree polynomial over a finite field is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]], then NEXP is not in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]].
  • If NEXP is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]], then NEXP is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]][[Complexity_Garden#permanent|Perm]].
Does not equal [[#np|NP]] [[zooref#sfm78|[SFM78]]]. Does not equal [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] if and only if there is a sparse set in [[#np|NP]] that is not in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. There exists an oracle relative to which [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] = NEXP but still [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] does not equal [[#np|NP]] [[zooref#dek76|[Dek76]]]. The theory of reals with addition (see [[Complexity Zoo:E#expspace|EXPSPACE]]) is hard for NEXP [[zooref#fr74|[FR74]]].

name: NEXP/poly
title: Nonuniform NEXP
body: Contains [[Complexity Zoo:C#conexp|coNEXP]] (folklore result reported in [https://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2004/01/little-theorem.html Fortnow's weblog]).

name: NIPZK
title: Non-Interactive PZK
body: Defined in [[zooref#m08|[M08]]] based on [[zooref#ddp98|[DDPY98]]],[[zooref#bfm88|[BFM88]]]. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:P#pzk|PZK]] and co[[Complexity Zoo:S#sbp|SBP]]. There are oracles separating [[Complexity Zoo:N#nipzk|NIPZK]] from [[Complexity Zoo:P#pzk|PZK]], co[[Complexity Zoo:N#nipzk|NIPZK]], and [[Complexity Zoo:S#sbp|SBP]] [[zooref#bchtv17|[BCHTV17]]], [[zooref#dgpv20|[DGPV20]]]. [[zooref#m08|[M08]]] showed a complete promise-problem for NIPZK, called Uniform (UN). Instances in UN are circuits with n+1 output bits. The first n bits represent the uniform distribution, and the last bit is 1 with probability at least 2/3. For instances not in UN, when the last bit is 1, at most 1/3 of the strings of length n can appear as the output of the circuit. The problem is to decide which is the case. [[zooref#dgpv20|[DGPV20]]] showed Uniform is in co[[Complexity Zoo:S#sbp|SBP]].

name: NIQSZK
title: Non-Interactive QSZK
body: Has the same relation to [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qszk|QSZK]] as [[#niszk|NISZK]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]]. Defined in [[zooref#kob02|[Kob02]]], where it was also shown that the following promise problem is complete for NIQSZK. Given a quantum circuit, we are promised that the state it prepares (when run on the all-0 state, and tracing out non-output qubits) has trace distance either at most 1/3 or at least 2/3 from the maximally mixed state. The problem is to output "no" in the former case and "yes" in the latter. NIQPZK can be defined similarly.

name: NISZK
title: Non-Interactive SZK
body:
Defined in [[zooref#ddp98|[DDP+98]]]. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]]. [[zooref#gsv99|[GSV99]]] showed the following:
  • If [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]] does not equal [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] then NISZK does not equal [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]].
  • NISZK equals [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]] if and only if NISZK is closed under complement.
  • NISZK has natural complete promise problems:
    • Statistical Distance from Uniform (SDU): Given a circuit, consider the distribution over outputs when the circuit is given a uniformly random n-bit string. We're promised that the trace distance between this distribution and the uniform distribution is either at most 1/3 or at least 2/3. The problem is to output "yes" in the former case and "no" in the latter.
    • Entropy Approximation (EA): Now we're promised that the entropy of the circuit's output distribution is either at least k+1 or at most k-1. The problem is to output "yes" in the former case and "no" in the latter.
NIPZK can be defined similarly. There is an oracle separating NISZK from [[Complexity Zoo:P#pp|PP]] [[zooref#bchtv17|[BCHTV17]]].

name: NISZK_h
title: NISZK With Limited Help
body:
The non-interactive analogue of [[Complexity Zoo:S#szkh|SZKh]]. Defined in [[zooref#bg03|[BG03]]], where the following was also shown:
  • NISZKh contains [[#niszk|NISZK]] and is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]].
  • [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|Graph Isomorphism]] is in NISZKh.
  • The following problem is complete for NISZKh: Given two functions from {0,1}n to {0,1}n (specified by circuits), decide whether their ranges are almost equal or almost disjoint, given that one of these is the case.
The quantum lower bound for the set comparison problem in [[zooref#aar02|[Aar02]]] implies an oracle relative to which NISZKh is not in [[Complexity Zoo:B#bqp|BQP]].

name: NL
title: Nondeterministic Logarithmic-Space
body: NL is to [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] as [[#np|NP]] is to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Not known whether a particular relation (equality or inequality) between P and NP implies the same relation between L and NL. In a breakthrough result, was shown to equal [[Complexity Zoo:C#conl|coNL]] [[zooref#imm88|[Imm88]]] [[zooref#sze87|[Sze87]]]. (Though contrast to [[Complexity Zoo:M#mnl|mNL]].) Is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:L#logcfl|LOGCFL]] [[zooref#sud78|[Sud78]]], as well as [[#nc2|NC<sup>2</sup>]]. Is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:U#ulpoly|UL/poly]] [[zooref#ra00|[RA00]]]. Deciding whether a bipartite graph has a perfect matching is hard for NL [[zooref#kuw86|[KUW86]]]. NL can be defined in a logical formalism as [[Complexity_Zoo:S#sokrom|SO(krom)]] and also as [[Complexity_Zoo:F#fotc|FO(tc)]], reachability in directed graph is NL-Complete under FO-reduction.

name: NLIN
title: Nondeterministic LIN
body: Has the same relation to [[Complexity Zoo:L#lin|LIN]] as [[#np|NP]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]].

name: NLO
title: NL Optimization Problems
body: The class of optimization problems which can be solved in nondeterministic logspace. Defined in [[zooref#tan07|[TAN07]]] as the logspace equivalent of [[#npo|NPO]], where it is shown that the various logspace approximation classes form a hierarchy iff [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] ≠ [[#nl|NL]]. As with the definition of [[#npo|NPO]] in [[zooref#acg99|[ACG+99]]], NLO is defined as a class of "structured" problems, comprising both a "solution relation" (indicating which solutions are acceptable for a given input) and a "measure function" (computing the value of each solution). The equivalent "unstructured" class is [[Complexity Zoo:O#optl|OptL]]. See [[zooref#tan07|[TAN07]]] for discussion.

name: NLOG
title: NL With Nondeterministic Oracle Tape
body: Same as [[#nl|NL]] -- but if there's an oracle, then NLOG can make queries nondeterministically on a polynomial-size, one-way oracle tape. ([[#nl|NL]], by contrast, can use nondeterministic transitions only on the worktape; oracle queries have to be deterministic.) See [[zooref#ll76|[LL76]]] or [[zooref#hck88|[HCK+88]]] for more information. Although NLOG is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]], there exists an oracle relative to which that is not the case. This illustrates that care is needed when defining oracle access mechanisms.

name: NL/poly
title: Nonuniform NL
body: Has the same relation to [[#nl|NL]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Is contained in [[#paritylpoly|⊕L/poly]] [[zooref#gw96|[GW96]]], as well as [[#sac1|SAC<sup>1</sup>]]. Equals [[Complexity Zoo:U#ulpoly|UL/poly]] [[zooref#ra00|[RA00]]].

name: NLT
title: Nearly Linear Time
body: Class of functions computable in nearly linear time n(log n)<sup>O(1)</sup> on deterministic random access machines. Defined in [[zooref#gs89|[GS89]]]. See also [[Complexity Zoo:Q#ql|QL]].

name: NMCL
title: Nondeterministic Moore-Crutchfield Languages
body: Alternative name for [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qrl|QRL]]. Named such in <ref>Abuzer Yakaryilmaz, A. C. Cem Say. Languages recognized by nondeterministic quantum finite automata. https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.2081</ref>. Not to be confused with the similar [[#nql_2|NQL]].

name: NNC(''f(n)'')
title: NC with ''O(f(n))'' nondeterministic gates
body: Same as [[#nc|NC]], but with ''O(f(n))'' nondeterministic gates. A nondeterministic gate has no inputs and a single output bit. Defined in [[zooref#wol94|[Wol94]]], where the author proves various inclusions, including but not limited to NNC(poly(n))=[[#np|NP]], NNC(log(n))=[[#nc|NC]], and NNC(polylog)⊆[[Complexity Zoo:D#dspace|DSPACE]](polylog).

name: NNLT
title: Nondeterministic Nearly Linear Time
body: Class of functions computable in nearly linear time n(log n)<sup>O(1)</sup> on nondeterministic random access machines. Equals [[#nql|NQL]] [[zooref#gs89|[GS89]]]. Defined in [[zooref#gs89|[GS89]]].

name: NONE
title: The Empty Class
body: The class that does not contain any languages. (It might not surprise you that I put this one in at the suggestion of a mathematician...) Is the opposite of [[Complexity Zoo:A#all|ALL]], but does not equal the complement [[Complexity Zoo:A#all|coALL]] = [[Complexity Zoo:A#all|ALL]]. Is closed under polynomial-time Turing reductions :-). Equals [[Complexity Zoo:S#sparse|SPARSE]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:C#cosparse|coSPARSE]] and [[Complexity Zoo:T#tally|TALLY]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:T#tally|coTALLY]].

name: NP
title: Nondeterministic Polynomial-Time
body:
The class of dashed hopes and idle dreams. More formally: an "NP machine" is a nondeterministic polynomial-time Turing machine. Then NP is the class of decision problems solvable by an NP machine such that
  1. If the answer is "yes," at least one computation path accepts.
  2. If the answer is "no," all computation paths reject.
Equivalently, NP is the class of decision problems such that, if the answer is "yes," then there is a proof of this fact, of length polynomial in the size of the input, that can be verified in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] (i.e. by a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm). On the other hand, if the answer is "no," then the algorithm must declare invalid any purported proof that the answer is "yes." For example, the [[Complexity_Garden#sat|SAT]] problem is to decide whether a given Boolean formula has any satisfying truth assignments. [[Complexity_Garden#sat|SAT]] is in NP, since a "yes" answer can be proved by just exhibiting a satisfying assignment. A decision problem is NP-complete if (1) it is in NP, and (2) any problem in NP can be reduced to it (under some notion of reduction). The class of NP-complete problems is sometimes called [[#npc|NPC]]. That NP-complete problems exist is immediate from the definition. The seminal result of Cook [[zooref#coo71|[Coo71]]], Karp [[zooref#kar72|[Kar72]]], and Levin [[zooref#lev73|[Lev73]]] is that many natural problems (that have nothing to do with Turing machines) are NP-complete. The first such problem to be shown NP-complete was [[Complexity_Garden#sat|SAT]] [[zooref#coo71|[Coo71]]]. Other classic NP-complete problems include:
  • '''3-Colorability''': Given a graph, can each vertex be colored red, green, or blue so that no two neighboring vertices have the same color?
  • '''Hamiltonian Cycle''': Given a graph, is there a cycle that visits each vertex exactly once?
  • '''Traveling Salesperson''': Given a set of n cities, and the distance between each pair of cities, is there a route that visits each city exactly once before returning to the starting city, and has length at most T?
  • '''Maximum Clique''': Given a graph, are there k vertices all of which are neighbors of each other?
  • '''Subset Sum''': Given a collection of integers, is there a subset of the integers that sums to exactly x?
For many, many more NP-complete problems, see [[zooref#gj79|[GJ79]]]. There exists an oracle relative to which [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] and NP are unequal [[zooref#bgs75|[BGS75]]]. Indeed, [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] and NP are unequal relative to a random oracle with probability 1 [[zooref#bg81|[BG81]]] (see [[zooref#afm01|[AFM01]]] for a novel take on this result). Though random oracle results are not always indicative about the unrelativized case [[zooref#ccg94|[CCG+94]]]. There even exists an oracle relative to which the [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] versus NP problem is outside the usual axioms of set theory [[zooref#hh76|[HH76]]]. If we restrict to monotone classes, [[Complexity Zoo:M#mp|mP]] is strictly contained in [[Complexity Zoo:M#mnp|mNP]] [[zooref#raz85|[Raz85]]]. Perhaps the most important insight anyone has had into [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] versus NP is to be found in [[zooref#rr97|[RR97]]]. There the authors show that no 'natural proof' can separate [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] from NP (or more precisely, place NP outside of [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]]), unless secure pseudorandom generators do not exist. A proof is 'natural' if it satisfies two conditions called constructivity and largeness; essentially all lower bound techniques known to date satisfy these conditions. To obtain unnatural proof techniques, some people suspect we need to relate [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] versus NP to heavy-duty 'traditional' mathematics, for instance algebraic geometry. See [[zooref#ms02|[MS02]]] (and the survey article [[zooref#reg02|[Reg02]]]) for a development of this point of view. For more on

name: NPC
title: NP-Complete
body:
The class of decision problems such that (1) they're in [[#np|NP]] and (2) every problem in [[#np|NP]] is reducible to them (under some notion of reduction). In other words, the hardest problems in [[#np|NP]]. Two notions of reduction from problem A to problem B are usually considered:
  1. Karp or many-one reductions. Here a polynomial-time algorithm is given as input an instance of problem A, and must produce as output an instance of problem B.
  2. Turing reductions, in this context also called Cook reductions. Here the algorithm for problem B can make arbitrarily many calls to an oracle for problem A.
Some examples of NP-complete problems are discussed under the entry for [[#np|NP]]. The classic reference on NPC is [[zooref#gj79|[GJ79]]]. Unless [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[#np|NP]], NPC does not contain any sparse problems: that is, problems such that the number of 'yes' instances of size n is upper-bounded by a polynomial in n [[zooref#mah82|[Mah82]]]. A famous conjecture [[zooref#bh77|[BH77]]] asserts that all NP-complete problems are polynomial-time isomorphic -- i.e. between any two problems, there is a one-to-one and onto Karp reduction. If that's true, the NP-complete problems could be interpreted as mere "relabelings" of one another. NP-complete problems are p-superterse unless [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[#np|NP]] [[zooref#bks95|[BKS95]]]. This means that, given k Boolean formulas F1,...,Fk, if you can rule out even one of the 2k possibilities in polynomial time (e.g., "if F1,...,Fk-1 are all unsatisfiable then Fk is satisfiable"), then [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[#np|NP]].

name: NP_C
title: NP Over The Complex Numbers
body: An analog of [[#np|NP]] for Turing machines over a complex number field. Defined in [[zooref#bcs97|[BCS+97]]]. It is unknown whether [[Complexity Zoo:P#pc|P<sub>C</sub>]] = NP<sub>C</sub>, nor are implications known among this question, [[Complexity Zoo:P#pr2|P<sub>R</sub>]] versus [[#npr|NP<sub>R</sub>]], and [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] versus [[#np|NP]]. However, [[zooref#ckk95|[CKK+95]]] show that if [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] does not equal [[#nppoly|NP/poly]] then [[Complexity Zoo:P#pc|P<sub>C</sub>]] does not equal NP<sub>C</sub>. [[zooref#bcs97|[BCS+97]]] show the following striking result. For a positive integer n, let t(n) denote the minimum number of additions, subtractions, and multiplications needed to construct n, starting from 1. If for every sequence {n<sub>k</sub>} of positive integers, t(n<sub>k</sub> k!) grows faster than polylogarithmically in k, then [[Complexity Zoo:P#pc|P<sub>C</sub>]] does not equal NP<sub>C</sub>. See also [[Complexity Zoo:V#vnp|VNP<sub>k</sub>]].

name: NP^cc
title: Communication Complexity NP
body: The analogue of [[Complexity Zoo:P#pcc|P<sup>cc</sup>]] for nondeterministic communication complexity. Both communication bits and nondeterministic guess bits count toward the complexity. Does not equal [[Complexity Zoo:P#pcc|P<sup>cc</sup>]] or [[Complexity Zoo:C#conpcc|coNP<sup>cc</sup>]] because of the [[Complexity Garden#equality|EQUALITY]] problem. Also, does not contain [[Complexity Zoo:B#bppcc|BPP<sup>cc</sup>]] because of that problem. Is not contained in [[Complexity Zoo:B#bppcc|BPP<sup>cc</sup>]] (first shown by [[zooref#bfs86|[BFS86]]]). SET-INTERSECTION, in which Alice's and Bob's strings are identified with characteristic vectors of sets and yes-inputs are intersecting while no-inputs are disjoint, is the canonical [[Complexity Zoo:N#npcc|NP<sup>cc</sup>]]-complete problem. Sometimes SET-DISJOINTNESS also refers to this problem, but sometimes it refers to the complement of this problem. The complexity measure corresponding to NP<sup>cc</sup> is equivalent to the log of the number of rectangles needed to cover exactly the set of 1-entries of the communication matrix.

name: NPI
title: NP-Intermediate
body: Sometimes used to denote the set of decision problems in [[#np|NP]] that are neither NP-complete (that is, in [[#npc|NPC]]) nor in [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Is thought to contain (for example) decision versions of factoring and [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|graph isomorphism]]. Is nonempty if [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] does not equal [[#np|NP]] [[zooref#lad75|[Lad75]]]. Indeed, under this assumption, it contains an infinite number of distinct polynomial-time equivalence classes.

name: NP ∩ coNP
title: The intersection of NP and coNP
body: The class of problems in both [[#np|NP]] and [[Complexity Zoo:C#conp|coNP]]. Contains [[Complexity_Garden#integer_factorization|factoring]] [[zooref#pra75|[Pra75]]]. Contains [[Complexity_Garden#graph_isomorphism|graph isomorphism]] under the assumption that some language in [[#ne|NE]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:C#cone|coNE]] requires nondeterministic circuits of size 2<sup>Ω(n)</sup> ([[zooref#mv99|[MV99]]], improving [[zooref#km99|[KM99]]]). (A nondeterministic circuit C has two inputs, x and y, and accepts on x if there exists a y such that C(x,y)=1.) Equals P<sup>NP ∩ coNP</sup> [[zooref#bra79|[Bra79]]]. In particular, if a problem in NP ∩ coNP is NP-hard with Turing reduction, then NP = coNP. Is not believed to contain complete problems. Is equal to Low(NP)={L : NP<sup>L</sup>=NP} [[zooref#sch83|[Sch83]]].

name: (NP ∩ coNP)/poly
title: Nonuniform NP ∩ coNP
body: Together with [[#nppoly|NP/poly ∩ coNP/poly]], has the same relation to [[#npiconp|NP ∩ coNP]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] has to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. A language in (NP ∩ coNP)/poly is defined by a single language in [[#npiconp|NP ∩ coNP]] which is then modified by advice. A language in [[#nppoly|NP/poly ∩ coNP/poly]] comes from two possibly different languages in [[#np|NP]] and [[Complexity Zoo:C#conp|coNP]] which become the same with good advice. There is an oracle relative to which [[#nppoly|NP/poly ∩ coNP/poly]], indeed NP/1 ∩ coNP/1, is not contained in (NP ∩ coNP)/poly [[zooref#ffk93|[FFK+93]]]. Recently they improved this to NP/1 ∩ coNP [[zooref#ff..|[FF..]]]. If [[#np|NP]] is contained in (NP ∩ coNP)/poly, then [[Complexity Zoo:P#ph|PH]] collapses to [[Complexity Zoo:S#s2p|S<sub>2</sub>P]]<sup>[[#npiconp|NP ∩ coNP]]</sup> [[zooref#cch01|[CCH+01]]].

name: NP_^cc
title: NP^cc in NOF model, players
body: Has the same relation to [[#npcc|NP<sup>cc</sup>]] and [[#np|NP]] as {{zcls|p|pkcc|P<sub><math>k</math></sub><sup>cc</sup>}} does to {{zcls|p|pcc|P<sup>cc</sup>}} and {{zcls|p|p}}. NP<sub><math>k</math></sub><sup>cc</sup> is not contained in {{zcls|b|bppkcc|BPP<sub><math>k</math></sub><sup>cc</sup>}} for <math>k\le(1-\delta)\cdot\log n</math> players, for any constant <math>\delta>0</math>. As a result, NP<sub><math>k</math></sub><sup>cc</sup> is not equal to {{zcls|r|rpkcc|RP<sub><math>k</math></sub><sup>cc</sup>}} under the same conditions {{zcite|DP08}}.

name: NP/log
title: NP With Logarithmic Advice
body: Same as [[#nppoly|NP/poly]], except that now the advice string is logarithmic-size. Shown in [[zooref#fk05|[FK05]]] that [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] ⊆ NP/log if and only if [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] = [[Complexity Zoo:P#pparnp|P<sup>||NP</sup>]].

name: NPMV
title: NP Multiple Value
body: The class of all (possibly partial, possibly multivalued) functions computed by an [[#np|NP]] machine as follows: ignore the rejecting paths, and consider any output of an accepting path to be "one of the outputs." Contains [[#npsv|NPSV]] and [[#npmvt|NPMV<sub>t</sub>]]. Defined in [[zooref#bls84|[BLS84]]]. Contrast with [[Complexity Zoo:F#fnp|FNP]].

name: NPMV-sel
title: NPMV Selective
body: Has the same relation to [[#npmv|NPMV]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#psel|P-Sel]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Defined in [[zooref#hhn95|[HHN+95]]].

name: NPMV_t
title: NPMV Total
body: The class of all (possibly multivalued) [[#npmv|NPMV]] functions that are total (that is, defined for every input).

name: NPMV_t-sel
title: NPMV_t Selective
body: Has the same relation to [[#npmvt|NPMV<sub>t</sub>]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#psel|P-Sel]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Defined in [[zooref#hhn95|[HHN+95]]].

name: NPO
title: NP Optimization
body: The class of function problems of the form, "Find any n-bit string x that maximizes a cost function C(x), where C is computable in [[Complexity Zoo:F#fp|FP]] (i.e. polynomial-time)." Defined in [[zooref#acg99|[ACG+99]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:A#apx|APX]] and [[#npopb|NPOPB]].

name: NPOPB
title: NPO Polynomially Bounded
body: The subclass of [[#npo|NPO]] problems for which the cost function is guaranteed always to be bounded by a polynomial in n (the input size). See [[zooref#acg99|[ACG+99]]]. NPOPB equals the closure of [[Complexity Zoo:M#maxpb|MaxPB]] under [[Complexity Zoo:P#ptas|PTAS]] reductions [[zooref#cks99|[CKS+99]]].

name: NP/poly
title: Nonuniform NP
body: Has the same relation to [[#np|NP]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:A#am|AM]]. On the other hand, if NP/poly contains [[Complexity Zoo:C#conp|coNP]] then [[Complexity Zoo:P#ph|PH]] collapses to the third level. NP/poly-natural proofs cannot show that circuit families are outside [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]], under a pseudorandomness assumption [[zooref#rud97|[Rud97]]].

name: (NP,P-samplable)
title: Average NP With Samplable Distributions
body: See [[Complexity Zoo:A#avgp|AvgP]] for basic notions of average-case complexity. (NP,P-samplable) is the same as [[Complexity Zoo:D#distnp|DistNP]], except that the distribution μ only needs to be samplable in polynomial time. μ's cumulative density function does not need to be computable in polynomial time. Any problem complete for [[Complexity Zoo:D#distnp|DistNP]] is also complete for (NP,P-samplable) [[zooref#il90|[IL90]]].

name: NP_R
title: NP Over The Reals
body: An analog of [[#np|NP]] for Turing machines over a real number field. Defined in [[zooref#bcs97|[BCS+97]]]. It is unknown whether [[Complexity Zoo:P#pr2|P<sub>R</sub>]] = NP<sub>R</sub>, nor are implications known among this question, [[Complexity Zoo:P#pc|P<sub>C</sub>]] versus [[#npc2|NP<sub>C</sub>]], and [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] versus [[#np|NP]]. Also, in contrast to the case of [[#npc2|NP<sub>C</sub>]], it is an open problem to show that [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] distinct from [[#nppoly|NP/poly]] implies [[Complexity Zoo:P#pr2|P<sub>R</sub>]] distinct from NP<sub>R</sub>. The difference is that in the real case, a comparison (or greater-than) operator is available, and it is not known how much power this yields in comparison to the complex case. See also [[Complexity Zoo:V#vnp|VNP<sub>k</sub>]].

name: NPSPACE
title: Nondeterministic PSPACE
body: Equals [[Complexity Zoo:P#pspace|PSPACE]] [[zooref#sav70|[Sav70]]]. On the other hand, this result does not relativize if we allow strings of unbounded length to be written to the oracle tape. In particular, there exists an oracle relative to which NPSPACE is not contained in [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] [[zooref#gtw91|[GTW+91]]].

name: NPSV
title: NP Single Value
body: The class of [[#npmv|NPMV]] functions that are single-valued (i.e., such that every accepting path outputs the same value). Defined in [[zooref#bls84|[BLS84]]]. Contains [[#npsvt|NPSV<sub>t</sub>]]. [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] = [[#np|NP]] if and only if [[Complexity Zoo:F#fp|FP]] = NPSV.

name: NPSV-sel
title: NPSV Selective
body: Has the same relation to [[#npsv|NPSV]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#psel|P-Sel]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Defined in [[zooref#hhn95|[HHN+95]]].

name: NPSV_t
title: NPSV Total
body: The class of all [[#npsv|NPSV]] functions that are total (that is, defined on every input). Contained in [[#npmvt|NPMV<sub>t</sub>]].

name: NPSV_t-sel
title: NPSV_t Selective
body: Has the same relation to [[#npsvt|NPSV<sub>t</sub>]] as [[Complexity Zoo:P#psel|P-Sel]] does to [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]]. Also known as NP-sel. Defined in [[zooref#hhn95|[HHN+95]]].

name: NQL
title: Nondet Quasi-Linear
body: The class of problems that can be decided in quasi-linear time by a multitape nondeterministic Turing machine. Quasi-linear here means n(log n)<sup>k</sup> + k, for some k. Equals [[#nnlt|NNLT]]. SAT is NQL-complete under quasi-linear-time reductions (which can be computed in deterministic quasi-linear time) [[zooref#sch78|[Sch78]]]. Defined in [[zooref#sch78|[Sch78]]]. See also: [[#nlt|NLT]], [[Complexity Zoo:Q#q|Q]], [[Complexity Zoo:Q#ql|QL]]. Unrelated to [[#nql_2|the other NQL]] below.

name: NQL
title: Nondeterministic Quantum Languages
body: An unfortunate name collision. The class of problems nondeterministically recognized by ''Kondacs-Watrous Quantum Finite Automata''. These are automata that undergo a unitary transformation for each symbol consumed, and are measured after '''each''' step to check for acceptance or rejection. The "nondeterminism" refers to the fact that the automaton will accept with positive probability if in the language, or with exactly zero probability otherwise. Has the same caveats as [[#nqp|NQP]] and [[Complexity Zoo:E#eqp|EQP]] because of the exact acceptance probabilities. Initially studied in <ref>A. Kondacs; J. Watrous. On the power of quantum finite state automata. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/646094</ref>, where they show that it contains all regular languages. In <ref>Abuzer Yakaryılmaz and A.C. Cem Say. Languages recognized by nondeterministic quantum finite automata. https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.2081v2</ref> it was shown that this inclusion was strict. Also showed that NQL = [[Complexity Zoo:S#sneq|S<sup>≠</sup>]] Contrast with [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qrl|QRL]], which is a different model of quantum finite automaton, in which measurement only occurs at the end. Unrelated to [[#nql|the other NQL]] above.

name: NQP
title: Nondeterministic Quantum Polynomial-Time
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a QTM in polynomial time such that a particular '|Accept>' state has nonzero amplitude at the end of the computation, if and only if the answer is 'yes.' Since it has an exact amplitude condition, NQP has the same technical caveats as [[Complexity Zoo:E#eqp|EQP]]. Or it would, except that it turns out to equal [[Complexity Zoo:C#cocequalsp|coC<sub>=</sub>P]] [[zooref#fgh98|[FGH+98]]]. Defined in [[zooref#adh97|[ADH97]]]. Contrast with [[Complexity Zoo:Q#qma|QMA]].

name: NSPACE(f(n))
title: Nondeterministic f(n)-Space
body: Same as [[#npspace|NPSPACE]], but with f(n)-space (for some constructible function f) rather than polynomial-space machines. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:D#dspace|DSPACE]](f(n)<sup>2</sup>) [[zooref#sav70|[Sav70]]], and indeed [[Complexity Zoo:R#revspace|RevSPACE]](f(n)<sup>2</sup>) [[zoorefComplexity Zoo:C#cp|95|[CP95]]]. NSPACE(n<sup>k</sup>) is strictly contained in NSPACE(n<sup>k+ε</sup>) for ε>0 [[zooref#iba72|[Iba72]]] (actually the hierarchy theorem is stronger than this, but pretty technical to state).

name: NT
title: Near-Testable
body: The class of decision problems such that whether the answer on input x agrees with the answer on input x-1 (that is, the lexicographic predecessor of x) is solvable in polynomial time. The Turing machine has to decide agreement or disagreement without access to the answer for x-1. Is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:E#e|E]], [[#ntstar|NT*]], and [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]]. Defined in [[zooref#ghj91|[GHJ+91]]] to study [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]]-complete problems. They show that [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]], NT, [[#ntstar|NT*]], and [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]] are either all equal or strictly nested. In particular, they differ with probability 1 relative to a random oracle.

name: NTIME(f(n))
title: Nondeterministic f(n)-Time
body: Same as [[#np|NP]], but with f(n)-time (for some constructible function f) rather than polynomial-time machines. The Nondeterministic Time Hierarchy Theorem: If f and g are time-constructible and f(n+1)=o(g), then NTIME(f(n)) does not equal NTIME(g(n)) [[zooref#sfm78|[SFM78]]] (this is actually stronger than the hierarchy theorem for [[Complexity Zoo:D#dtime|DTIME]]). NTIME(n) strictly contains [[Complexity Zoo:D#dtime|DTIME(n)]] [[zooref#pps83|[PPS+83]]] (this result does not work for arbitrary f(n)). For any constructible superpolynomial f, NTIME(f(n)) with [[#np|NP]] oracle is not in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#kan82|[Kan82]]].

name: NT*
title: Near-Testable With Forest Ordering
body: Defined like NT, but with a more general ordering on inputs. A problem L is in NT* if, first, there is a partially defined predecessor function pred(x) in [[Complexity Zoo:F#fp|FP]] that organizes the space of inputs into a forest. The size of the lineage of each x must also be bounded by 2<sup>poly(|x|)</sup>. Second, if L(x) is the Boolean answer to L on input x, then L(x)+L(pred(x)) is computable in polynomial time; or if pred(x) does not exist, L(x) is computable in polynomial time. Defined in [[zooref#ghj91|[GHJ+91]]]. Contains [[#nt|NT]] and is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]]. The inclusions are either both strict or both equalities (whence [[Complexity Zoo:Symbols#parityp|⊕P]] = [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] as well).

name: OCL
title: One-Counter Languages
body: The class of languages accepted by nondeterministic one-counter automata: finite automata equipped with one nonnegative counter that can be incremented, decremented, and tested for zero. Equivalently, OCL is the class accepted by pushdown automata with a singleton stack alphabet, plus a bottom marker. REG ⊊ OCL ⊊ CFL. As decision problems over strings, OCL ⊆ NL. Examples include {a^n b^n : n ≥ 0} and the one-parenthesis Dyck language. The two-parenthesis Dyck language is CFL but not OCL. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:D#DOCL|DOCL]] and [[Complexity Zoo:P#PB-OCL|PB-OCL]]. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:C#CFL|CFL]] and [[Complexity Zoo:N#NL|NL]].

name: OIP
title: Oblivious IP
body:
[[Complexity Zoo:I#ip|IP]] where only the input size is known during the interaction with the prover, and after that interaction, the verifier gets the specific input. L is in OIP if there exists a randomized, polynomial time interrogator I which takes an input size and interacts with a prover to produce a witness, and polynomial time verifier V that takes an input and a witness so that
  1. Given an input size n, there is prover so that I given n and interacting with the prover produces a witness w so that, for any input x of length n where x is in L, V accepts on x and w.
  2. For any x not in L of length n, for any prover interacting with I on input n gives a witness w' which V will reject with x and w' with probability at least 2/3.
OIP = [[Complexity Zoo:I#ip|IP]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#gm15|[GM15]]].

name: OMA
title: Oblivious MA
body:
The class of functions computable in randomized polynomial time with a shared, untrusted witness for each input size. The input-oblivious version of [[Complexity Zoo:M#ma|MA]]. L is in OMA if there exists a randomized, polynomial time verifier V taking an input and a witness, so that:
  1. There is a witness for each n of polynomial size, so that for any input of size n, if the input is is in L, then the verifier accepts on that input and the witness.
  2. If the input is not in L, then for any witness, the verifier rejects on that input with probability at least 1/2.
[[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] is contained in OMA iff [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#fsw09|[FSW09]]]. [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] iff [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] = OMA [[zooref#fsw09|[FSW09]]]. [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] is contained in OMA [[zooref#gm15|[GM15]]]. Implicit in {{zcite|San07}} that OMA/1 (that is, OMA with 1 bit of trusted advice) does not have circuits of size n^k for any k>0.

name: ONP
title: Oblivious NP
body:
The class of functions computable in polynomial time with a shared, untrusted witness for each input size. The input-oblivious version of [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]]. L is in ONP if there exists a polynomial time verifier V taking an input and a witness, so that:
  1. There is a witness for each n of polynomial size, so that for any input of size n, if the input is in L, then the verifier accepts on that input and the witness.
  2. If the input is not in L, then for any witness, the verifier rejects on that input.
Defined in [[zooref#fsw09|[FSW09]]], where it was shown [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] has size nk circuits for some constant k if and only if ONP/1 has size nj circuits for some constant j. ONP is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] and [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] [[zooref#fsw09|[FSW09]]]. ONP = [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] iff [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] is in [[Complexity Zoo:P#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#fsw09|[FSW09]]]. If [[Complexity Zoo:N#ne|NE]] is not [[Complexity Zoo:E#e|E]] then ONP is not [[Complexity Zoo:P#p|P]] [[zooref#gm15|[GM15]]]. See also [[Complexity Zoo:Y#yp|YP]] for an input oblivious analogue of [[Complexity Zoo:N#npiconp|NP ∩ coNP]].

name: OptP
title: Optimum Polynomial-Time
body: The class of functions computable by taking the maximum (or minimum) of the output values over all accepting paths of an [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] machine. OptP[f(n)] restricts the size of the output to f(n) bits. Defined in [[zooref#kre88|[Kre88]]]. Contrast with [[Complexity Zoo:F#fnp|FNP]]. [[MaxSat]] that returns the number of satisfied clauses, [[Clicque]] that returns the size of the clique, [[Chromatic Number]] are OptP[log n]-complete.

name: k-PBP
title: Polynomial-Size Width-k Branching Program
body: A branching program is a directed acyclic graph with a designated start vertex. Each (non-sink) vertex is labeled by the name of an input bit, and has two outgoing edges, one of which is followed if that input bit is 0, the other if the bit is 1. A sink vertex can be either an 'accept' or a 'reject' vertex. The size of the branching program is the number of vertices. The branching program has width k if the vertices can be sorted into levels, each with at most k vertices, such that each edge goes from a level to the one immediately after it. Then k-PBP is the class of decision problems solvable by a family of polynomial-size, width-k branching programs. (A uniformity condition may also be imposed.) k-PBP equals (nonuniform) [[Complexity Zoo:N#nc1|NC1]] for constant k at least 5 [[zooref#bar89|[Bar89]]]. On the other hand, 4-PBP is in [[Complexity Zoo:A#acc0|ACC0]] [[zooref#bt88|[BT88]]]. Contained in k-[[Complexity Zoo:E#eqbp|EQBP]], as well as [[#pbp|PBP]]. See also [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpdp|BPd(P)]].

name: P
title: Polynomial-Time
body: The class that started it all. The class of decision problems solvable in polynomial time by a Turing machine. (See also [[Complexity Zoo:F#fp|FP]], for function problems.) Defined in [[zooref#edm65|[Edm65]]], [[zooref#cob64|[Cob64]]], [[zooref#rab60|[Rab60]]], and other seminal early papers. Contains some highly nontrivial problems, including linear programming [[zooref#kha79|[Kha79]]] and finding a maximum matching in a general graph [[zooref#edm65|[Edm65]]]. Contains the problem of testing whether an integer is prime [[zooref#aks02|[AKS02]]], an important result that improved on a proof requiring an assumption of the generalized Riemann hypothesis [[zooref#mil76|[Mil76]]]. A decision problem is P-complete if it is in P, and if every problem in P can be reduced to it in [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] (logarithmic space). The canonical P-complete problem is circuit evaluation: given a Boolean circuit and an input, decide what the circuit outputs when given the input. Important subclasses of P include [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]], [[Complexity Zoo:N#nl|NL]], [[Complexity Zoo:N#nc|NC]], and [[Complexity Zoo:S#sc|SC]]. P is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]], but whether they're equal seemed to be an open problem when I last checked. Efforts to generalize P resulted in [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] and [[Complexity Zoo:B#bqp|BQP]]. The nonuniform version is [[#ppoly|P/poly]], the monotone version is [[Complexity Zoo:M#mp|mP]], and versions over the real and complex number fields are [[#pr2|PR]] and [[#pc|PC]] respectively. In descriptive complexity, P can be defined by three different kind of formulae, [[#Complexity_Zoo:F#folfp|FO(lfp)]] which is also [[#Complexity_Zoo:F#fot|FO(n^{O(1)})]]], and also as [[#Complexity_Zoo:S#sohorn|SO(Horn)]] P queries are exactly the one that can be written in the [[Complexity_Zoo:W#while|While/cons]] languages. P is the class of decision problems solvable by a (logspace) ''uniform'' family of polynomial-size Boolean circuits. P can be computed by interactive protocols (see [[Complexity Zoo:I#ip|IP]]) where the verifier runs in log space (see [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]] and [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpl|BPL]]) [[zooref#gkr15|[GKR15]]].

name: PAC^0
title: Probabilistic AC^0
body: The Political Action Committee for computational complexity research. The class of problems for which there exists a [[Complexity Zoo:D#diffac0|DiffAC<sup>0</sup>]] function f such that the answer is "yes" on input x if and only if f(x)>0. Equals [[Complexity Zoo:T#tc0|TC<sup>0</sup>]] and [[Complexity Zoo:C#cequalsac0|C<sub>=</sub>AC<sup>0</sup>]] under logspace uniformity [[zooref#abl98|[ABL98]]].

name: para-
title: Parameterized Complexity
body: The para- prefix indicates that a complexity class is parameterized by some other measure of complexity. Specifically, a language L is in the parameterized class para-C, if there is an alphabet A and a computable function pi(k) -> A*, such that every (Q,k) is in para-L if and only if (Q,pi(k)) in L. The prototypical example (as well the violation of the naming convention) is para-P, which is almost always known as [[Complexity Zoo:FPT#fpt|FPT]], which is equal to DTIME(f(k)n^c) for some constant c. Space-parameterized examples include [[#para-L|para-L]] and [[#para-NL|para-NL]], which are equal to DSPACE(f(k)+log(n)) and NDSPACE(f(k)+log(n)), respectively. Compare with the slicewise complexity classes [[Complexity Zoo:X#x|X-]], such as [[Complexity Zoo:X#x|X-]]. Discussed in: J. Flum and M. Grohe. Describing parameterized complexity classes. Information and Computation. and Elberfeld M., Stockhusen C., Tantau T. (2012) On the Space Complexity of Parameterized Problems.

name: para-L
title: Parameterized Logspace
body: [[#para|para-]] version of [[Complexity Zoo:L#l|L]]. Equivalent to DSPACE(f(k)+log(n)) for some computable function f. Compare with slicewise parameterized logspace, [[Complexity Zoo:X#xl|XL]]. Parameterized vertex cover (is there a vertex cover of size at most k) is complete for para-L. (Elberfeld et al, 2012)

name: para-NL
title: Parameterized Nondeterministic Logspace
body: [[#para|para-]] version of [[Complexity Zoo:N#nl|NL]]. Equivalent to NDSPACE(f(k)+log(n)) for some computable function f. Compare with slicewise parameterized nondeterministic logspace, [[Complexity Zoo:X#xnl|XNL]]. It seems open whether there are natural complete problems for para-NL. However, the related class [[#paranlflog|para-NL[f log]]] has many natural complete problems.

name: para-NL[f log]
title: Parameterized Nondeterministic Logspace
body: Like [[#paranl|para-NL]], but where the number of nondeterministic branches is bounded by O(f(k) log(n)). A natural complete is problem parameterized distance: is there a path on directed graph G from vertex s to v, of length at most k? (Elberfeld et al, 2012) para-NL[f log] is contained within [[Complexity Zoo:X#xl|XL]], slicewise logspace.

name: para-P
title: Parameterized Polynomial time.
body: para-P is a less common name for [[Complexity Zoo:F#fpt|FPT]], but in line with other [[#para|para-]] classes naming conventions. Its slicewise counterpart is still called [[Complexity Zoo:X#xp|XP]].

name: PBP
title: Polynomial-Size Branching Program
body: Same as [[#kpbp|k-PBP]] but with no width restriction. Equals [[Complexity Zoo:L#l/poly|L/poly]] [[zooref#cob66|[Cob66]]]. Contains [[#pobdd|P-OBDD]], [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpdp|BP<sub>d</sub>(P)]].

name: P_C
title: Polynomial-Time Over The Complex Numbers
body: An analog of [[#p|P]] for Turing machines over a complex number field. Defined in [[zooref#bcs97|[BCS+97]]]. See also [[#pr2|P<sub>R</sub>]], [[Complexity Zoo:N#npc2|NP<sub>C</sub>]], [[Complexity Zoo:N#npr|NP<sub>R</sub>]], [[Complexity Zoo:V#vp|VP<sub>k</sub>]].

name: P^cc
title: Communication Complexity P
body: In a two-party communication complexity problem, Alice and Bob have n-bit strings x and y respectively, and they wish to evaluate some Boolean function f(x,y) using as few bits of communication as possible. P<sup>cc</sup> is the class of (infinite families of) f's, such that the amount of communication needed is only O(polylog(n)), even if Alice and Bob are restricted to a deterministic protocol. Note that all functions of the form above are solvable given <math>O(n)</math> bits of communication, since no bounds are placed on the computational abilities of Alice and Bob. Thus, when discussing this class, "polynomially" is sometimes used in place of "polylogarithmically." Is strictly contained in [[Complexity Zoo:N#npcc|NP<sup>cc</sup>]] and in [[Complexity Zoo:B#bppcc|BPP<sup>cc</sup>]] because of the [[Complexity Garden#equality|EQUALITY]] problem. If the classes are defined in terms of total functions, then P<sup>cc</sup> = [[Complexity Zoo:N#npcc|NP<sup>cc</sup>]] ∩ [[Complexity Zoo:N#npcc|coNP<sup>cc</sup>]] = [[Complexity Zoo:U#upcc|UP<sup>cc</sup>]]. Defined in [[zooref#bfs86|[BFS86]]].

name: PCD(r(n),q(n))
title: Probabilistically Checkable Debate
body: The class of decision problems decidable by a probabilistically checkable debate system, as follows. Two debaters B and C alternate writing strings on a "debate tape," with B arguing that the answer is "yes" and C arguing the answer is "no." Then a polynomial-time verifier flips O(r(n)) random coins and makes O(q(n)) nonadaptive queries to the debate tape (meaning that they depend only on the input and the random coins, not the results of previous queries). The verifier then outputs an answer, which should be correct with high probability. Defined in [[zooref#cfl93|[CFL+93]]], who also showed that PCD(log n, 1) = [[#pspace|PSPACE]]. This result was used to show that certain problems are [[#pspace|PSPACE]]-hard even to approximate. Contained in [[Complexity Zoo:G#gpcd|GPCD]](r(n),q(n)).

name: P-Close
title: Problems Close to P
body: The class of decision problems solvable by a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs the wrong answer on only a sparse (that is, polynomially-bounded) set of instances. Defined in [[zooref#yes83|[Yes83]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:A#almostp|Almost-P]] and is contained in [[#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#sch86|[Sch86]]].

name: PCP(r(n),q(n))
title: Probabilistically Checkable Proof
body:
The class of decision problems such that a "yes" answer can be verified by a probabilistically checkable proof, as follows. The verifier is a polynomial-time Turing machine with access to O(r(n)) uniformly random bits. It has random access to a proof (which might be exponentially long), but can query only O(q(n)) bits of the proof. Then we require the following:
  1. If the answer is "yes," there exists a proof such that the verifier accepts with certainty.
  2. If the answer is "no," then for all proofs the verifier rejects with probability at least 1/2 (over the choice of the O(r(n)) random bits).
Defined in [[zooref#as98|[AS98]]]. By definition [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] = PCP(0,poly(n)). [[Complexity Zoo:M#mip|MIP]] = PCP(poly(n),poly(n)). PCP(r(n),q(n)) is contained in [[Complexity Zoo:N#ntime|NTIME]](2O(r(n))q(n) + poly(n)). [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] = PCP(log n, log n) [[zooref#as98|[AS98]]]. In fact, [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] = PCP(log n, 1) [[zooref#alm98|[ALM+98]]]! On the other hand, if [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] is contained in PCP(o(log n), o(log n)), then [[#p|P]] = [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] [[zooref#fgl91|[FGL+91]]]. Also, even though there exists an oracle relative to which [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] = [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] [[zooref#hel84|[Hel84]]], if we could show there exists an oracle relative to which PCP(log n, 1) = [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]], then we'd have proved [[#p|P]] not equal to [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] [[zooref#for94|[For94]]]. Another weird oracle fact: since [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] does not equal [[Complexity Zoo:N#nexp|NEXP]] [[zooref#sfm78|[SFM78]]], PCP(log n, log n) does not equal PCP(poly(n), poly(n)). However, there exist oracles relative to which the latter inequality is false [[zooref#hcc92|[HCC+92]]].

name: P_CTC
title: P With Closed Time Curves
body: Same as [[#p|P]] with access to bits along a closed time curve. Implicitly defined in [[zooref#aar05c|[Aar05c]]], where it was shown that PSPACE = P<sub>CTC</sub>. See also [[Complexity Zoo:B#bqpctc|BQP<sub>CTC</sub>]].

name: PDQP
title: Product Dynamical Quantum Polynomial time
body: This class is a generalization of [[Complexity Zoo:B#bqp|BQP]] where one is allowed to perform measuresments without collapsing the wavefunction.[[zooref#abfl14|[ABFL14]]] Unlike, BQP this is likely to be a not physically realizable class. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:S#szk|SZK]] and thus contains graph isomorphism. There is an oracle relative to which BQP is not equal to PDQP and an oracle relative to which NP is not contained in PDQP. PDQP can perform unordered searches faster than BQP. Compare [[Complexity Zoo:D#dqp|DQP]].

name: PermUP
title: Self-Permuting UP
body: The class of languages L in [[Complexity Zoo:U#up|UP]] such that the mapping from an input x to the unique witness for x is a permutation of L. Contains [[#p|P]]. Defined in [[zooref#ht03|[HT03]]], where it was also shown that the closure of PermUP under polynomial-time one-to-one reductions is [[Complexity Zoo:U#up|UP]]. On the other hand, they show that if PermUP = [[Complexity Zoo:U#up|UP]] then [[Complexity Zoo:E#e|E]] = [[Complexity Zoo:U#ue|UE]]. See also: [[Complexity Zoo:S#selfnp|SelfNP]].

name: PEXP
title: Probabilistic Exponential-Time
body: Has the same relation to [[Complexity Zoo:E#exp|EXP]] as [[#pp|PP]] does to [[#p|P]]. Is not contained in [[#ppoly|P/poly]] [[zooref#bft98|[BFT98]]].

name: PFCHK(t(n))
title: Proof-Checker
body:
The class of decision problems solvable in time O(t(n)) by a nondeterministic Turing machine, as follows. The machine is given oracle access to a proof string of unbounded length.
  • If the answer is "yes," then there exists a value of the proof string such that all computation paths accept.
  • If the answer is "no," then for all values of the proof string, there exists a computation path that rejects.
Credited in [[zooref#for94|[For94]]] to S. Arora, R. Impagliazzo, and U. Vazirani. An interesting question is whether [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] = PFCHK(log n) relative to all possible oracles. Fortnow [[zooref#for94|[For94]]] observes that the answer depends on what oracle access mechanism is used.

name: PH
title: Polynomial-Time Hierarchy
body:
Let Δ0P = Σ0P = Π0P = [[#p|P]]. Then for i>0, let
  • ΔiP = [[#p|P]] with Σi-1P oracle.
  • ΣiP = [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] with Σi-1P oracle.
  • ΠiP = [[Complexity Zoo:C#conp|coNP]] with Σi-1P oracle.
Then PH is the union of these classes for all nonnegative constants i. PH can also be defined using alternating quantifiers: it's the class of problems of the form, "given an input x, does there exist a y such that for all z, there exists a w ... such that φ(x,y,z,w,...)," where y,z,w,... are polynomial-size strings and φ is a polynomial-time computable predicate. It's not totally obvious that this is equivalent to the first definition, since the first one involves adaptive [[Complexity Zoo:N#np|NP]] oracle queries and the second one doesn't, but it is. Defined in [[zooref#sto76|[Sto76]]]. Contained in [[#p|P]] with a [[#pp|PP]] oracle [[zooref#tod89|[Tod89]]]. Contains [[Complexity Zoo:B#bpp|BPP]] [[zooref#lau83|[Lau83]]]. Relative to a random oracle, PH is strictly contained in [[#pspace|PSPACE]] with probability 1 [[zooref#cai86|[Cai86]]]. Furthermore, there exist oracles separating any ΣiP from Σi+1P. In fact, relative to a random oracle, the hierarchy is infinite: each level is strictly contained in the next, with probability 1 [[zooref#rst15|[RST15]]] (this was an open problem for 29 years). Previously, it had been known that if it had collapsed relative to a random oracle, then it would have collapsed unrelativized [[zooref#boo94|[Boo94]]]. It was shown in [[zooref#cp07|[CPO7]]] that if the NP Machine Hypothesis holds, then \mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{SAT}[1]} = \mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{SAT}[2]} \Rightarrow \mathsf{PH} \subseteq \mathsf{NP} . For a compendium of problems complete for different classes of the Polynomial Hierarchy see [[zooref#sch02a|[Sch02a]]] and [[zooref#sch02b|[Sch02b]]]. PH is equal to the set of boolean queries recognizable by a concurent random acess machine using exponentially many processors and constant time[[zooref#imm89|[Imm89]]]. Since NP is the class of query expressible in second-order existantial logic, PH can also be defined as the query expressible in [[#Complexity_Zoo:S#so|second-order logic]].

name: PH^cc
title: Communication Complexity PH
body: The polynomial hierarchy for communication complexity, naturally built with [[Complexity Zoo:N#npcc|NP<sup>cc</sup>]] and [[Complexity Zoo:C#conpcc|coNP<sup>cc</sup>]] forming the first level. Specifically, a cost-k protocol in the PH<sup>cc</sup> model corresponds to a constant-depth 2<sup>k</sup>-ary tree whose internal nodes are alternating layers of AND and OR gates, and whose leaves represent (the indicator functions of) either rectangles or complements of rectangles, as appropriate. It is unknown whether Σ<sub>2</sub><sup>cc</sup> equals Π<sub>2</sub><sup>cc</sup>. Defined in [[zooref#bfs86|[BFS86]]], where it was also shown (among other things) that [[Complexity Zoo:B#bppcc|BPP<sup>cc</sup>]] is contained in Σ<sub>2</sub><sup>cc</sup> ∩ Π<sub>2</sub><sup>cc</sup>.

name: Φ_2P
title: Second Level of the Symmetric Hierarchy, Alternative Definition
body:
